title: The quasi-finite locus of a locally finite type algebraic space map
statement: Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space], schemes use [def-pc-scheme], and universes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Their point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]; fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Locally of finite type is tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a map $h:E\to T$ to a scheme, quasi-finite at $x\in|E|$ means that for every representable etale scheme chart $U\to E$ and every $u\in U$ above $x$, the scheme map $U\to T$ is quasi-finite at $u$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Let $S$ be a scheme, $E$ an algebraic space over $S$, and $h:E\to S$ locally of finite type. The set $Q_h=\{x\in|E|:h\text{ is quasi-finite at }x\}$ is open in $|E|$, and is the point set of an open subspace (its inclusion becomes an open immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-open-immersion]). For every scheme morphism $S^{\prime}\to S$, its inverse image in $E\times_SS^{\prime}$ is exactly the quasi-finite locus of $E\times_SS^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $p:U\to E$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $f=hp$. It is locally of finite type by the chartwise hypothesis. By [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open], its quasi-finite locus $V\subseteq U$ is open and $V\to S$ is locally quasi-finite. Set $O=p(V)$. The point map of $p$ is open by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], so $O$ is open. We will prove $O=Q_h$, including the identity $p^{-1}(Q_h)=V$.

proof.text: Let $a:A\to E$ be any representable etale scheme chart and set $A_O=a^{-1}(O)$, an open subscheme by continuity. Form $W=V\times_E A$. It is a scheme by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]: $V\to E$ is representable etale, since each scheme test is the open restriction of the corresponding test of $U\to E$, hence etale by [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction]. Both projections $W\to V$ and $W\to A$ are etale. The image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] says that the second projection has image $A_O$. Its factorization $W\to A_O$ is surjective etale, using [lem-a1-etale-open-restriction]. By [lem-a1-scheme-lqf-etale-source-locality], $W\to S$ is locally quasi-finite, as its factor $V\to S$ is; the converse of that same lemma for $W\to A_O$ then gives local quasi-finiteness of $A_O\to S$. Its affine witnesses are affine opens also in $A$, so [pqf-def-quasifinite] makes $A\to S$ quasi-finite at every point over $O$. Since $a$ was arbitrary, $O\subseteq Q_h$. Conversely, for $x\in Q_h$ every lift in the atlas $U$ is in $V$ by the definition of $Q_h$; there is a lift by surjectivity on points. Hence $Q_h\subseteq O$, and the same two implications give $p^{-1}(Q_h)=V$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-space-invariant-open-quotient] to $O=Q_h$ and the atlas $U\to E$. It constructs an algebraic space $J$ with point image $Q_h$ and inclusion representable by open immersions. This proves precisely the asserted open-subspace clause, with no separation or quasi-compactness assumption.

proof.text: Let $b:S^{\prime}\to S$ be arbitrary and put $E^{\prime}=E\times_SS^{\prime}$ and $U^{\prime}=U\times_SS^{\prime}$. By [lem-a1-space-lqf-atlas-refinement], $p^{\prime}:U^{\prime}\to E^{\prime}$ is a representable surjective etale atlas. Its composite $f^{\prime}:U^{\prime}\to S^{\prime}$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. The argument of Steps 1 and 2 uses only local finite type of the chosen atlas composite and scheme etale locality; it therefore applies to $p^{\prime}$ and identifies $(p^{\prime})^{-1}(Q_{h^{\prime}})$ with the scheme quasi-finite locus $V^{\prime}$ of $f^{\prime}$. By [lem-sfb-scheme-quasifinite-at-base-change], $V^{\prime}$ is the inverse image of $V$ under $U^{\prime}\to U$. Step 2 gives $V=p^{-1}(Q_h)$, so the inverse images in $U^{\prime}$ of $Q_{h^{\prime}}$ and of the inverse image of $Q_h$ in $E^{\prime}$ agree. Surjectivity of $|p^{\prime}|$ now gives equality of those subsets in $|E^{\prime}|$. For the corresponding open subspaces the base change of $J$ has this inverse-image point set, and uniqueness follows from the inclusion criterion in [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus].

lean.statement: theorem isOpen_mapToSchemeQuasiFiniteAt {S : Scheme.{u}} (T : Over S) (E : AlgebraicSpace S) (h : E.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hft : MapToSchemeIsLocally (@LocallyOfFiniteType) E T h) : IsOpen {x : Point E.obj.obj | MapToSchemeQuasiFiniteAt h x} ∧ (∃ J : OpenSubspace E, pointImage J.val.ι = {x : Point E.obj.obj | MapToSchemeQuasiFiniteAt h x}) ∧ ∀ (T' : Over S) (b : T' ⟶ T), mapPoint (Limits.pullback.fst h (yoneda.map b)) ⁻¹' {x : Point E.obj.obj | MapToSchemeQuasiFiniteAt h x} = {x : Point (Limits.pullback h (yoneda.map b)) | MapToSchemeQuasiFiniteAt (Limits.pullback.snd h (yoneda.map b)) x}
